articles.title: People who are more considerate of others show less “me first” bias in quick decisions
articles.summary: People usually recognize their own belongings faster than someone else’s, even when the items are just pens and pencils. A study found this self-bias was weaker among people who were more attentive to others’ needs and choices.

articles.title: People with darker personalities tend to prefer partners like themselves, study suggests

articles.title: Brain connectivity patterns map onto sensory processing styles in autistic youth

articles.title: Does loving horror make you psychologically tougher in a crisis? Not in war-torn Lebanon, study finds

articles.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup. The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.

articles.title: Women’s attention to beauty isn’t limited to the sex they’re attracted to, eye-tracking study finds

articles.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

articles.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago

The findings could help explain why harmful thought patterns are so difficult to break and offer new insights into treating mental disorders.
